q: How are steel plant waste gases sent to a power plant treated under CBAM?
title: Steel waste gas to power under CBAM
short: Blast furnace, COREX and converter gases carry carbon from the steel process. Under the CBAM monitoring rules their CO2 is attributed to the steel production process, with a correction for the electricity the gas generates. Keep metered gas volumes and composition to apply it.
audience: Integrated steel plants in Karnataka, Odisha and Jharkhand that burn process gases in captive power plants

p: The carbon in waste gas comes from coke or coal used to make iron. Without a rule, emissions could be shifted to the power plant and out of the steel figure.

ul: Volume of each waste gas exported to the power plant, from flow meters.
Gas composition or net calorific value from regular analysis.
Electricity and steam produced from it.

p: The exact correction is set in the CBAM implementing rules on calculating embedded emissions, which are amended from time to time. Confirm the version in force for your reporting year with your verifier.
